title: Langfuse Pricing 2026: Free Tier, Plans and What You Pay
summary: Langfuse pricing ranges from free to $2,499 monthly, with costs based on billable units not tier. Determine which plan offers the best per-unit pricing.
body_markdown:
## Watching Langfuse Usage with Activepieces


Set up a daily check that compares your monthly event count with what your plan includes. That way you hear about an overage while you can still change something.


Activepieces, a workflow automation tool, can do this in four steps: a schedule, an HTTP call to Langfuse's API, a condition, and a message.


A run is 1 credit however many steps it has, so a daily check costs about 30 credits a month, against the 1,000 credits on the free plan.


Nothing here replaces Langfuse or its billing page. Activepieces reads your usage and tells you when the gap between used and included is closing, which is the question the pricing page can't answer for you.


Its core is MIT-licensed and can be self-hosted, so the check can sit next to a self-hosted Langfuse as easily as a cloud one.


Check first whether Langfuse offers a native integration, or whether one of the 746 integrations in the Activepieces open source monorepo already covers usage monitoring. If one exists, use it and skip the HTTP step. If not, the generic HTTP step does the job.


### The example workflow and stage 1


In the screenshot, the same shape of flow appears with a different trigger: a Stripe "Payment Failed" event feeding a Slack "Send Message To A Channel" action. The run details show the first step completed and a "Run succeeded" notice at the bottom.


Take from it the structure and the run log, not the Stripe part. Swap the trigger for a schedule and the Slack step stays as it is, and the run log tells you whether each day's check actually executed.


For stage 1, a scheduled trigger that runs daily, use the schedule trigger and set it to run once a day.


A daily cadence is enough because usage accrues across a billing period, not in minutes, and a check that fires more often only adds runs for you to count.


Pick a time after your busiest traffic window so the figure you read reflects most of the day.


### Stage 2: pull usage from the Langfuse API


Add an HTTP step that calls Langfuse's API with your project keys as credentials. Keep the keys in a central Activepieces connection rather than pasting them into each step, so credentials live in one place and rotating them updates every flow that uses them.


On the Ultimate and enterprise-control tiers, secret managers are part of the feature set, so the keys can live in your own manager rather than in Activepieces' database.


Request the usage or event count for the current billing period, and confirm in Langfuse's API reference which endpoint and fields return billable units. Don't assume a metrics endpoint counts the same thing your invoice does.


Compare one day's output against the usage page in the Langfuse dashboard before you trust the workflow.


### Stage 3: alert at 80 percent of included units


Add a condition that divides units used by units included in your plan and continues only when the result reaches eighty percent. Enter the included amount from your plan's pricing page as a fixed value in the step.


If you change plans, update it, or the alert will measure against the wrong ceiling.


On the true branch, add a Slack or email step that states the units used, the units included, and the date. Eighty percent leaves time to prune noisy traces, lower sampling, or move plans before the bill reflects it.
